Scoped

The scope protocol behind with (var x = scope) { ... } else { ... }.

A with block holds scope in a hidden local, binds x to scope.enter(), and runs the body. When enter() returns a struct reference that is null, the body is skipped and the optional else block runs instead. Both locals are released on every path out of the block (falling off the end, return, break, continue), the binding first. Cleanup is the scope object’s destructor, which calls exit().

Source: runtime/scoped.pep

Scoped

trait Scoped<T>

Something a with block can enter.

enter() runs once when the block is entered, and its result is what the header binds. exit() is the cleanup: implementations call it from their destructor (destruct { this.exit(); }), so it runs when the scope object’s last reference is released. For a scope object created in the with header that is the end of the block; for one that is also held elsewhere, it is when that last owner lets go.

A with block with no binding (with (scope) { ... }) still holds the result of enter() until the block ends. An enter() that returns void has nothing to bind.

Type parameters

  • T — the type enter() returns

Example

    var open = 0;

    struct Session {
        construct() {
            open = open + 1;
        }

        destruct {
            this.exit();
        }

        Session enter() {
            return this;
        }

        exit() {
            open = open - 1;
        }
    }

    extend Session with Scoped<Session> {}

    main(): int {
        with (var session = Session()) {
            # open == 1 here
        }
        return open;   # 0: the session was destroyed at the end of the block
    }

Methods

enter

enter(): T

Enters the scope.

A null struct reference means there is nothing to use: the with body is skipped and its else block runs instead.

Returns

  • the value the with header binds

exit

exit()

Leaves the scope. Implementations call it from their destructor.

Weak

Weak references: Weak<T> points at an object without keeping it alive.

Source: runtime/weak.pep

Weak

struct Weak<T>

A reference to a struct object that does not keep it alive, for back pointers (a child’s parent, an observer’s subject) that would otherwise form a reference cycle and leak.

The object is reached only through a with block, which upgrades the weak reference to an ordinary strong one for the length of the block. Once the object has been destroyed the upgrade fails: the body is skipped and the else block runs instead.

A Weak<T> never changes what it points at, so copies of it can be shared freely.

Type parameters

  • T — the struct type pointed at

See also

  • Scoped

Example

    struct Child {
        Weak<Parent> owner;

        construct(Parent owner) {
            this.owner = Weak<Parent>(owner);
        }

        String owner_name() {
            with (var parent = this.owner) {
                return parent.name;
            } else {
                return "(gone)";
            }
            return "";
        }
    }

Constructor

Weak()

construct(target: T)

Creates a weak reference to target’s object.

Parameters

  • target — the object to point at; a null reference makes a weak reference that is always expired

Methods

expired

expired(): bool

Reports whether the object has been destroyed.

A false result can be out of date by the time it is used; enter the reference with with to use the object.

Returns

  • true once the object has been destroyed, or if the reference was made from null

enter

enter(): T

Upgrades the weak reference for a with block.

Returns

  • a new strong reference to the object, or null once it has been destroyed

exit

exit()

Leaves the scope. The strong reference enter() returned is released by the with block itself, so there is nothing to do.

Source: runtime/result.pep

Error

struct Error

The default error type of Result: a human-readable message.

Example

    var r = Result<int>.err(Error("boom"));
    var n = r.error().message.length();   # 4

Fields

message

String message

The description of what went wrong; empty when none was given.

Constructor

Error()

[Implicit] construct(message: String = "")

Creates an Error carrying message.

The constructor is [Implicit]: a String converts to an Error wherever an Error is expected, as in Result<int>.err("bad input").

Parameters

  • message — the description of the failure; defaults to the empty string

Result

enum Result<TValue, TError=Error>

The outcome of an operation that can fail: either Ok, holding a TValue, or Err, holding a TError, like Rust’s Result<T, E>.

An enum with the cases Ok(value) and Err(error). Build one with a case (Result<int>.Ok(42)) or the static ok or err functions, and read it with match or is (if (r is Err(e)) { ... }), or with is_ok(), is_err(), value() and error(); value() and error() panic on the wrong kind of result. TError defaults to Error, so Result<int> is Result<int, Error>.

Result<void> is the result of an operation that returns nothing on success, like Rust’s Result<(), E>. A void type argument erases what it types: that instance’s Ok carries nothing (Result<void>.Ok, and the pattern Ok), ok() takes no argument, and value() returns nothing, so it only checks that the result is Ok.

Type parameters

  • TValue — the type of the value an Ok result carries; void when there is none
  • TError — the type of the error an Err result carries; defaults to Error

Example

    main(): int {
        var a = Result<int>.ok(42);
        if (a.value() != 42) { return 1; }
        var b = Result<int>.err(Error("boom"));
        if (!b.is_err()) { return 2; }
        var n = match (b) { Ok(v) => v, Err(e) => e.message.length() };   # 4
        return b.ok_or(0);   # 0
    }

The operation succeeded with value.

Parameters

  • value — the success value

The operation failed with error.

Parameters

  • error — the failure value

For Result<void>, ok() takes no argument.

Parameters

Returns

Optional

Source: runtime/optional.pep

Optional

struct Optional<T>

A value of type T that may be absent: either Some, holding a T, or None, holding nothing, like Rust’s Option<T> and Swift’s Optional.

Use it instead of a null reference or a sentinel (-1, "") wherever a value may be missing: the type says so, and reading the value goes through value(), which checks, or value_or(), which cannot fail. It works for every type, including those that have no null, such as int.

T? is shorthand for Optional<T>, and a variable or field of an optional type that is not given a value starts as None.

Build one with the static some or none functions, or Optional<T>() for None, and test it with is_some() or is_none(), or as a condition by itself (if (found)).

Type parameters

  • T — the type of the value a Some optional holds

Example

    find_even(values: Array<int>): int? {
        for (var v in values) {
            if (v % 2 == 0) { return Optional<int>.some(v); }
        }
        return Optional<int>.none();
    }

    main(): int {
        var values = Array<int>();
        values.append(3);
        values.append(4);
        var found = find_even(values);
        if (!found) { return 1; }
        return found.value() - 4;   # 0
    }

construct()

Creates a None optional, one holding no value.

Example

    var nothing = Optional<int>();   # nothing.is_none() == true

For a struct T the optional acquires a reference to value.

Returns a None optional, one holding no value; the same as Optional<T>().

The io module

Files, directories, paths, and sockets, modeled on Rust’s std::fs, std::path and std::net.

Unlike the rest of the standard library, io is a module: bring it in with import io (and write io.File, io.Path) or import names directly with import [File, Path] from io. Every fallible operation returns an IoResult<T>, a Result whose error is an IoError.

  • Path: building, splitting, and inspecting paths
  • File: opening, reading, and writing files, and whole-file helpers
  • Directory: listing, creating, and removing directories
  • Network addresses: IpAddress, SocketAddress, and resolve
  • Sockets: TcpListener, SharedTcpListener, TcpStream, SocketTransfer, and UdpSocket
  • Unix domain sockets: UnixListener, SharedUnixListener, and UnixStream
  • Errors and platform types: IoError, IoResult, and handle types

Example

    import io;

    main(): int {
        var path = io.Directory.temp().join("greeting.txt");
        assert(io.File.write_text(path, "hello").is_ok(), "write");
        assert(io.File.read_to_string(path).value() == "hello", "read back");
        io.File.remove(path);
        return 0;
    }

Source: runtime/io/module.pep

Errors and platform types

Source: runtime/io/types.pep

FileHandle

[Target(!OS(Windows))] type FileHandle = int

The raw operating-system handle of an open file: a POSIX file descriptor.

File.Handle holds one. A valid descriptor is >= 0; a File that is closed (or was never opened) holds -1. The standard streams are descriptors 0, 1 and 2. On Windows this is a HANDLE instead.

See also

  • File

Note

  • code that must build for every target should not rely on this being an int

SocketHandle

[Target(!OS(Windows))] type SocketHandle = int

The raw operating-system handle of a socket: a POSIX file descriptor.

TcpListener, TcpStream and UdpSocket hold one. A valid descriptor is >= 0; a closed socket holds -1. On Windows this is a SOCKET instead.

See also

  • TcpStream

Note

  • code that must build for every target should not rely on this being an int

ErrorCode

[Target(!OS(Windows))] type ErrorCode = int

The raw platform error code carried by IoError.code: a POSIX errno value such as ENOENT (2). On Windows this is a DWORD from GetLastError() instead.

The numbers differ between platforms (and a few between Linux and macOS), so portable code classifies an error with the IoError predicates (is_not_found(), …) rather than comparing codes.

See also

  • IoError

Mode

[Target(!OS(Windows))] type Mode = uint

File mode bits as reported in Metadata.Permissions: on POSIX the mode_t permission bits mode & 07777 (the rwx bits for owner, group and others plus setuid, setgid and sticky; the file-type bits are removed). On Windows the same field holds FILE_ATTRIBUTE_* bits instead.

See also

  • Metadata

FileHandle

[Target(OS(Windows))] type FileHandle = __ptr<void>

The raw operating-system handle of an open file: a Windows HANDLE.

File.Handle holds one. A File that is closed (or was never opened) holds null; neither null nor INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE (-1) is a valid handle. The standard streams are the handles from GetStdHandle. On POSIX this is an int file descriptor instead.

See also

  • File

Note

  • code that must build for every target should not rely on this being a __ptr<void>

SocketHandle

[Target(OS(Windows))] type SocketHandle = ulong

The raw operating-system handle of a socket: a Winsock SOCKET, an unsigned pointer-sized integer.

TcpListener, TcpStream and UdpSocket hold one. A closed socket holds INVALID_SOCKET (all bits set). On POSIX this is an int file descriptor instead.

See also

  • TcpStream

Note

  • code that must build for every target should not rely on this being a ulong

ErrorCode

[Target(OS(Windows))] type ErrorCode = uint

The raw platform error code carried by IoError.code: a Windows DWORD error code from GetLastError(), such as ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (2). On POSIX this is an errno value instead.

The numbers differ between platforms, so portable code classifies an error with the IoError predicates (is_not_found(), …) rather than comparing codes.

See also

  • IoError

Mode

[Target(OS(Windows))] type Mode = uint

File attribute bits as reported in Metadata.Permissions: on Windows the whole FILE_ATTRIBUTE_* word of the file (FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY is 1, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY 16, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT 1024, …). On POSIX the same field holds mode_t permission bits instead.

See also

  • Metadata

Offset

type Offset = long

A byte position or distance within a file, as taken and returned by the File.seek* methods: a signed 64-bit integer on every target (off_t on POSIX, LARGE_INTEGER on Windows), so files larger than 4 GiB work everywhere.

IoError

struct IoError

An I/O failure: the raw platform error code plus a human-readable message.

There are no enums, so the kind of error is a set of predicates over the code (is_not_found(), is_permission_denied(), …), each of which knows the matching codes on the current platform. Test with those rather than comparing code against numbers. Failures that Pepper detects itself (invalid UTF-8, an empty path, a short write, a closed File) use the platform’s own code for the kind they are (EINVAL / ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER for invalid input, ENOENT / ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND for an empty path, …), so the predicates hold for them too. A short write uses EIO / ERROR_WRITE_FAULT and a closed File uses EBADF / ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE; no predicate matches those.

See also

  • IoResult

Example

    import io;

    var r = io.File.open(io.Path("settings.txt"));
    if (r.is_err()) {
        if (r.error().is_not_found()) {
            print("no settings file");
        } else {
            print(r.error().message);
        }
    }

Fields

code

ErrorCode code

The raw platform error code: an errno value on POSIX, a GetLastError() code on Windows; 0 means no error.

message

String message

A human-readable description: the platform’s text for code (strerror on POSIX, FormatMessageW on Windows, without its trailing period and line break), or Pepper’s own text such as "empty path" for errors it detects itself.

Constructor

IoError()

construct(code: ErrorCode = 0, message: String = "")

Creates an error from a platform code and a message.

The default, IoError(), has code 0 and an empty message; no predicate holds for it.

Parameters

  • code — the raw platform error code (errno on POSIX, GetLastError() on Windows)
  • message — the human-readable description

Static methods

last

static last(): IoError

Captures the calling thread’s last platform error now: errno on POSIX, GetLastError() on Windows, with the platform’s message for it.

Call it immediately after the failing system call; any call in between (including one that allocates) may overwrite the code.

Returns

  • an error holding the current errno / GetLastError() code and its message

Methods

is_not_found

is_not_found(): bool

Returns whether the error means the file or directory does not exist.

Matches ENOENT on POSIX, and ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND or ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND on Windows. An empty path fails with this kind on POSIX (with the message "empty path"), and in File.open_with on every platform.

resolve and TcpStream.connect_host fail with this kind too when a host name has no address.

Returns

  • true when a path, or a directory on the way to it, is missing, or a host name has no address

is_permission_denied

is_permission_denied(): bool

Returns whether the operation was refused for lack of permission.

Matches EACCES or EPERM on POSIX, and ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED on Windows (which Windows also reports for, among others, deleting a read-only file).

Returns

  • true when access was denied

is_already_exists

is_already_exists(): bool

Returns whether the operation failed because its target already exists, such as Directory.create on an existing path or opening with create_new.

Matches EEXIST on POSIX, and ERROR_FILE_EXISTS or ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the target already exists

is_not_a_directory

is_not_a_directory(): bool

Returns whether a path that had to name a directory names something else, such as Directory.open or Directory.remove on a file (or, on POSIX, a file used as a directory in the middle of a path).

Matches ENOTDIR on POSIX, and ERROR_DIRECTORY (267, “the directory name is invalid”) on Windows.

Returns

  • true when a directory was expected

is_is_a_directory

is_is_a_directory(): bool

Returns whether an operation that needs a file was given a directory, such as reading from a directory opened as a File.

Matches EISDIR on POSIX, and ERROR_DIRECTORY_NOT_SUPPORTED on Windows (which File reads report for a directory handle).

Returns

  • true when a directory was given where a file was expected

is_directory_not_empty

is_directory_not_empty(): bool

Returns whether a directory could not be removed because it still has entries (Directory.remove on a non-empty directory).

Matches ENOTEMPTY on POSIX (39 on Linux, 66 on macOS) and ERROR_DIR_NOT_EMPTY on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the directory is not empty

is_invalid_input

is_invalid_input(): bool

Returns whether an argument was invalid: bad options (such as opening with no access mode), data that is not valid UTF-8 where text was expected, or a malformed path.

Matches EINVAL on POSIX, and ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER or ERROR_INVALID_NAME on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the input was invalid

is_interrupted

is_interrupted(): bool

Returns whether the operation was interrupted before it finished.

Matches EINTR on POSIX and ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED on Windows. The io functions retry interrupted POSIX opens, reads and writes themselves, so callers rarely see this.

Returns

  • true when the operation was interrupted

is_connection_refused

is_connection_refused(): bool

Returns whether a connection attempt was refused: nothing listens on that port (the peer answered with a reset).

Matches ECONNREFUSED on POSIX and WSAECONNREFUSED on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the connection was refused

is_connection_reset

is_connection_reset(): bool

Returns whether an established connection was broken by the peer: reset, aborted, or (when writing) already closed.

Matches ECONNRESET, ECONNABORTED or EPIPE on POSIX, and WSAECONNRESET or WSAECONNABORTED on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the connection was reset or closed by the peer

is_address_in_use

is_address_in_use(): bool

Returns whether binding failed because another socket already uses the address and port.

Matches EADDRINUSE on POSIX and WSAEADDRINUSE on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the address is in use

is_address_not_available

is_address_not_available(): bool

Returns whether an address cannot be used here: binding to an IP address that is not one of this machine’s, or connecting to port 0.

Matches EADDRNOTAVAIL on POSIX and WSAEADDRNOTAVAIL on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the address is not available

is_timed_out

is_timed_out(): bool

Returns whether an operation gave up because the peer did not answer in time, such as a connection attempt to an unreachable host, or because an async.timeout scope around it expired.

Matches ETIMEDOUT on POSIX and WSAETIMEDOUT on Windows.

Returns

  • true when the operation timed out

is_cancelled

is_cancelled(): bool

Returns whether an operation stopped because the task waiting for it was cancelled (see async.Task.cancel).

Matches ECANCELED on POSIX, and ERROR_OPERATION_ABORTED or ERROR_CANCELLED on Windows.

Returns

  • true when cancellation ended the operation

IoResult

type IoResult<T> = Result<T, IoError>

The result of an io operation: a value on success, an IoError on failure. Check is_ok() / is_err() before calling value() or error(); operations that produce nothing return IoResult<void>.

Type parameters

  • T — the value an operation produces on success

See also

  • IoError

Example

    import io;

    var cwd = io.Directory.current();
    if (cwd.is_ok()) {
        print(cwd.value().to_string());
    } else {
        print(cwd.error().message);
    }

Path

Source: runtime/io/path.pep

Path

struct Path

An owned file-system path: the text of the path plus operations on it (Rust’s Path and PathBuf in one type).

Every method except exists, is_file, is_dir, metadata, symlink_metadata and canonicalize is pure text manipulation: it never touches the file system, so .. is not resolved against symlinks and nothing needs to exist. “No path” is the empty Path (there is no Option): parent() of a root, for example, is Path("").

Separators: on POSIX only / separates components (\ is an ordinary byte of a name). On Windows both / and \ separate, and a path may start with a prefix: a drive (C:) or a UNC share (\\server\share). Methods that build a path (join, normalize, with_extension) insert the platform separator (separator()), but the rest of the text is kept as written. Paths are UTF-8 Strings, scanned byte by byte; separators and dots are ASCII, so splitting at them never cuts a character in two.

Example

    import io;

    var p = io.Path("docs").join("guide.md");   # "docs/guide.md"
    var name = p.file_name();                       # "guide.md"
    var ext = p.extension();                        # "md"
    var dir = p.parent();                           # io.Path("docs")
    if (p.is_file()) {
        print(p.to_string());
    }

Constructor

Path()

[Implicit] construct(value: String = "")

Creates a path holding value as is: no validation, normalization or separator conversion.

The constructor is [Implicit]: a String (or a string literal) converts to a Path wherever a Path is expected, so every API that takes a Path also accepts text.

Parameters

  • value — the path’s text; the default, "", is the empty path

Example

    import io;

    var p = io.Path("/usr/lib");
    var empty = io.Path();   # is_empty() is true
    var q: io.Path = "docs";   # converted implicitly

Static methods

separator

static separator(): String

Returns the separator this platform inserts when it builds a path.

Returns

  • "/" on POSIX, "\" on Windows (where / is also accepted as a separator on input)

dot_index

static dot_index(name: String): ulong

Returns the byte offset of the dot that starts the extension in the file name name: the last . that is not the first byte. A leading dot (.bashrc) starts the name, not an extension.

Parameters

  • name — a file name (one component, as file_name() returns)

Returns

  • the index of the extension’s dot, or name.size when the name has no extension (including the empty name)

Methods

to_string

to_string(): String

Returns the path’s text, the same String the Path holds, not a copy.

Returns

  • the path as a String

is_empty

is_empty(): bool

Returns whether the path has no text at all. The empty path means “no path”: it is what parent() returns for a root or a bare name, and file-system operations on it fail.

Returns

  • true when the path’s text is ""

is_absolute

is_absolute(): bool

Returns whether the path is absolute, meaning it does not depend on the current directory. Pure text: the path need not exist.

On POSIX a path is absolute when it starts with /. On Windows it is absolute when it has a drive followed by a root separator (C:\x, C:/x) or is a UNC path (\\server\share\x); a root without a drive (\x) and a drive without a root (C:x) are both relative. The empty path is relative.

Returns

  • true when the path is absolute

is_relative

is_relative(): bool

Returns whether the path is relative: the opposite of is_absolute(). The empty path is relative.

Returns

  • true when the path is not absolute

join

join(other: Path): Path

Returns this path with other appended as further components.

A platform separator is inserted between the two unless this path already ends in one. If other is absolute, or (on Windows) starts with a root separator or a drive or UNC prefix, it replaces this path instead, as in Rust. Joining an empty other returns a copy of this path; joining onto the empty path returns other. Nothing is normalized: a joined with ../b is a/../b.

Parameters

  • other — the path to append

Returns

  • a new Path; this path is not changed

Example

    import io;

    var p = io.Path("usr").join(io.Path("lib"));   # "usr/lib" ("usr\lib" on Windows)
    var q = io.Path("a/").join(io.Path("b"));      # "a/b"
    var r = io.Path("a").join(io.Path("/abs"));    # "/abs"
    var so = io.Path("usr").join("lib").join("x.so");   # a String converts to a Path

join_str

[Deprecated("use 'join', which accepts a String", "join")] join_str(other: String): Path

Returns this path with the String other appended, exactly like join(Path(other)). Deprecated: join accepts a String directly, since a String converts to a Path implicitly.

Parameters

  • other — the path text to append

Returns

  • a new Path; this path is not changed

See also

  • join

Example

    import io;

    var so = io.Path("usr").join("lib").join("x.so");   # "usr/lib/x.so"

has_root_or_prefix

has_root_or_prefix(): bool

Returns whether the path starts with a root separator or, on Windows, a drive or UNC prefix. This is what makes join replace instead of append; unlike is_absolute() it is also true for Windows paths such as \x and C:x. On POSIX it equals is_absolute().

Returns

  • true when the path has a root separator or a prefix

parent

parent(): Path

Returns the path without its last component. Pure text: .. is not resolved, so the parent of a/.. is a.

Trailing and repeated separators before the last component are dropped (a/b/ and a//b both give a). The parent of a top-level name keeps the root and prefix (/a gives /, C:\x gives C:\, C:x gives C:).

Returns

  • the parent path, or the empty path for a root (/, C:\), a bare name (a, ., ..), or the empty path

Example

    import io;

    var p = io.Path("/a/b/c.txt").parent();   # "/a/b"
    var root = io.Path("/a").parent();        # "/"
    var none = io.Path("/").parent();         # "" (empty)

file_name

file_name(): String

Returns the last component of the path, ignoring trailing separators (a/b/ gives b).

Returns

  • the last component, or "" for a root, the empty path, or a path whose last component is . or ..

Example

    import io;

    var name = io.Path("/a/b/c.txt").file_name();   # "c.txt"
    var none = io.Path("a/..").file_name();         # ""

file_stem

file_stem(): String

Returns the file name without its extension: everything before the last dot, unless that dot is the first character.

Returns

  • the stem (c.tar for c.tar.gz, .bashrc for .bashrc, foo for foo.), or "" when there is no file name (see file_name())

extension

extension(): String

Returns the file name’s extension, without its dot: the text after the last dot, unless that dot is the first character. Only the file name counts; a dot in a directory name (a.b/c) is not an extension.

Returns

  • the extension (gz for c.tar.gz), or "" when there is none (noext, .bashrc, foo.) or no file name

with_extension

with_extension(ext: String): Path

Returns this path with its file name’s extension replaced by ext, added when it has none, or removed when ext is empty. Trailing separators after the file name are dropped.

Parameters

  • ext — the new extension without a leading dot (a dot is inserted; ".md" would give b..md), or "" to remove the extension

Returns

  • the new path, or a copy of this path unchanged when it has no file name (a root, ., .., or the empty path)

Example

    import io;

    var md = io.Path("a/b.txt").with_extension("md");   # "a/b.md"
    var rs = io.Path("a/b").with_extension("rs");       # "a/b.rs"
    var bare = io.Path("a/b.txt").with_extension("");   # "a/b"

components

components(): Array<String>

Returns the path split into its components: the prefix (Windows drive or UNC share, such as C:), then the root separator (one character, as written), then each non-empty part between separators.

Repeated and trailing separators produce no empty parts. . parts are dropped, except a leading one in a path with no prefix or root (./a gives . and a). .. parts are kept as they are.

Returns

  • the components in order; empty for the empty path

Example

    import io;

    var c = io.Path("/usr//lib/./x/").components();   # ["/", "usr", "lib", "x"]
    var d = io.Path("./a/b").components();            # [".", "a", "b"]

normalize

normalize(): Path

Returns the path cleaned up lexically, without touching the file system: . parts and repeated or trailing separators are dropped, and each .. removes the part before it.

A .. cannot climb above a root (/../x gives /x) and is kept at the start of a relative path (../a/.. gives ..). The prefix is kept, and every separator becomes the platform separator. Because symlinks are not consulted, link/.. becomes . even when link points elsewhere; use canonicalize() for the path the file system resolves.

Returns

  • the normalized path; . when the path cleans to nothing (a/.., ./), and the empty path for the empty path

See also

  • canonicalize

Example

    import io;

    var p = io.Path("a/./b/../c").normalize();   # "a/c" ("a\c" on Windows)
    var q = io.Path("a/..").normalize();         # "."

exists

exists(): bool

Returns whether something exists at this path, following symlinks. A relative path is resolved against the current directory.

Any error counts as not existing: a dangling symlink, a path under a directory that cannot be read, and the empty path all give false. Use metadata() to tell those apart.

Returns

  • true when the path (or a symlink’s target) can be stat’ed

is_file

is_file(): bool

Returns whether the path names a regular file, following symlinks.

Returns

  • true for a regular file or a symlink to one; false for anything else, and on any error (including a missing path)

is_directory

is_directory(): bool

Returns whether the path names a directory, following symlinks.

Returns

  • true for a directory or a symlink to one; false for anything else, and on any error (including a missing path)

is_dir

[Deprecated("use 'is_directory' instead", "is_directory")] is_dir(): bool

Deprecated: use is_directory instead. Returns whether the path names a directory, following symlinks.

Returns

  • the same as is_directory()

metadata

metadata(): IoResult<Metadata>

Returns the metadata of the file or directory at this path, following symlinks: the result describes the target (so on POSIX is_symlink is always false). stat / statx on POSIX; on Windows the path is opened for attributes only.

Returns

  • the Metadata of the path (or of a symlink’s target); an error when the path cannot be stat’ed: is_not_found() when it (or a symlink’s target) is missing or the path is empty, is_permission_denied() when a directory on the way cannot be searched, and on POSIX is_not_a_directory() when a file is used as a directory in the middle of the path

See also

  • symlink_metadata

Example

    import io;

    var m = io.Path("data.bin").metadata();
    if (m.is_ok()) {
        var size = m.value().size;
    }

symlink_metadata

symlink_metadata(): IoResult<Metadata>

Returns the metadata of the path itself without following a symlink at the end of it, so for a symlink is_symlink is true and the rest describes the link rather than its target. lstat / statx with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW on POSIX; on Windows the path is opened with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, and any reparse point (junctions included) reports is_symlink, together with is_directory for a directory link. For anything that is not a symlink it equals metadata().

Returns

  • the Metadata of the path itself; an error as for metadata(), except that a dangling symlink succeeds

See also

  • metadata

canonicalize

canonicalize(): IoResult<Path>

Returns the absolute path the file system resolves this path to: relative to the current directory, with every symlink, . and .. resolved. Unlike normalize(), the path must exist.

POSIX uses realpath. Windows opens the path and asks for its final name; the result uses \, and the \\?\ prefix Windows reports is removed (\\?\UNC\server\share becomes \\server\share).

Returns

  • the canonical absolute path; an error when the path cannot be resolved: is_not_found() when it (or a symlink’s target) is missing or the path is empty, is_permission_denied() when a directory on the way cannot be searched

See also

  • normalize

Example

    import io;

    var real = io.Path("a/../b.txt").canonicalize();
    if (real.is_ok()) {
        print(real.value().to_string());
    }

operator ==

==(rhs: Path): bool

Returns whether two paths have exactly the same text. The comparison is byte by byte, with no normalization and case-sensitive on every platform: a/b differs from a//b, from a/b/, and (on Windows) from a\b and A/b. Compare normalize() or canonicalize() results to ignore spelling differences.

Parameters

  • rhs — the path to compare with

Returns

  • true when both paths’ texts are equal

operator !=

!=(rhs: Path): bool

Returns whether two paths differ in their text: the opposite of ==, with the same byte-by-byte comparison.

Parameters

  • rhs — the path to compare with

Returns

  • true when the paths’ texts differ

File

Source: runtime/io/file.pep

OpenOptions

struct OpenOptions

Describes how File.open_with (or OpenOptions.open) opens a file: which access it asks for, and whether the file is created or truncated.

A builder in the style of Rust’s std::fs::OpenOptions. A new OpenOptions has every option off; each setter stores its flag and returns this same OpenOptions, so calls chain. The rules, checked when the file is opened:

  • At least one of read, write or append must be set, or opening fails with is_invalid_input().
  • create, create_new and truncate need write or append, or opening fails with is_invalid_input().
  • append implies write access, and every write goes to the current end of the file whatever the position; it wins over write.
  • create opens an existing file as it is (combine with truncate to empty it) and creates a missing one.
  • create_new creates the file and fails with is_already_exists() when it already exists, atomically (O_EXCL on POSIX, CREATE_NEW on Windows); create is then irrelevant.
  • truncate empties an existing file on open.
  • Without create or create_new, a missing file fails with is_not_found().

On POSIX a created file gets mode 0666 less the process umask, and the descriptor is opened close-on-exec. On Windows every file is opened sharing read, write and delete access with other openers.

See also

  • File.open_with

Example

    var r = OpenOptions().read(true).write(true).create(true).open(Path("data.bin"));
    if (r.is_err()) {
        return 1;
    }
    var f = r.value();

Constructor

OpenOptions()

construct()

Creates an OpenOptions with every option off. Set at least one of read, write or append before opening.

Sets whether the file is opened for reading.

Returns

Sets append mode: the file is opened for writing and every write goes to the current end of the file, whatever the position (seeking still moves the position for reads). Implies write access, and takes precedence over write.

Returns

create

Sets whether a missing file is created. An existing file is opened as it is unless truncate is also set. Requires write or append.

Parameters

Returns

create_new

create_new(v: bool): OpenOptions

Sets whether the file must be newly created: opening fails with is_already_exists() when the path already exists. The check and the creation are one atomic step. Requires write or append.

Parameters

Returns

open

open(path: Path): IoResult<File>

Opens path with these options. The same as File.open_with(path, this).

Parameters

  • path — the file to open

Returns

  • the open File, positioned at the start; an error when the options break a rule (is_invalid_input()), the path is empty or missing (is_not_found()), it exists under create_new (is_already_exists()), or the system refuses (is_permission_denied() and others)

See also

  • File.open_with

Example

    var log = OpenOptions().append(true).create(true).open(Path("log.txt")).value();
    log.write_all("started");

Metadata

struct Metadata

Describes a file system object: its kind, size, read-only flag, permission bits and timestamps, as a snapshot taken when it was queried.

Returned by File.metadata(), Path.metadata() (which follows symlinks), Path.symlink_metadata() (which does not) and DirEntry.metadata(). The timestamps are nanoseconds since the Unix epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC). On POSIX the metadata comes from statx (Linux) or stat (macOS); on Windows from GetFileInformationByHandle.

Example

    var m = Path("notes.txt").metadata();
    if (m.is_ok() && m.value().is_file) {
        var bytes = m.value().size;
    }

Fields

size

ulong size

The file’s length in bytes.

is_file

bool is_file

Whether this is a regular file. On Windows, anything that is neither a directory nor a reparse point (symlink) counts as a file.

is_directory

bool is_directory

Whether this is a directory.

is_symlink

bool is_symlink

Whether this is a symbolic link itself. Only metadata that does not follow links (Path.symlink_metadata()) can report one. On Windows this is any reparse point (FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT), which includes junctions.

read_only

bool read_only

Whether the file is read-only: on POSIX, no write permission bit (0222) is set for anyone; on Windows, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY is set.

modified

long modified

The time of the last modification of the contents, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.

accessed

long accessed

The time of the last access, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch (file systems mounted with noatime or relatime update it rarely or never).

created

long created

The creation (birth) time, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch; 0 where unavailable, such as on Linux file systems that do not record one.

permissions

Mode permissions

The raw permission bits: on POSIX the mode_t permission bits (mode & 07777, for example 256 for owner read); on Windows the FILE_ATTRIBUTE_* bits.

Constructor

Metadata()

construct()

Creates a Metadata with every field zero or false. Metadata is normally obtained from a query such as File.metadata().

File

[NotCopyable( "owns an operating-system handle and cannot be copied; send its path, and open the file again on the receiving thread" )] struct File

An open file, or a standard stream, read and written through its platform handle (a file descriptor on POSIX, a HANDLE on Windows).

Open one with File.open (read-only), File.create (write-only, created or truncated), or File.open_with / OpenOptions.open for anything else. The static conveniences read_bytes, read_to_string, write_bytes, write_text, copy, rename and remove work on a whole file by path.

I/O is unbuffered: each read and write is one system call. Reads and writes start at the current position and move it forward; the seek_* methods move it explicitly. A write to a standard stream first flushes the output print has buffered, so the two never come out of order.

Closing: the File’s destructor closes an owned handle when the last reference to the File is released, and ignores any error. Call close() to close earlier or to observe the error. The standard streams (stdin(), stdout(), stderr()) are never closed by a File. Every operation on a closed File fails with an error that none of the IoError predicates identify (EBADF on POSIX, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE on Windows).

Errors are IoError values carrying the platform’s code; use its predicates (is_not_found(), is_permission_denied(), …) to tell kinds apart portably.

Example

    var f = File.create(Path("out.txt")).value();
    f.write_all("hello");
    f.close();
    var text = File.read_to_string(Path("out.txt")).value();   # "hello"

Fields

path

Path path

The path the File was opened with; <stdin>, <stdout> or <stderr> for a standard stream, and empty for a File() never opened.

Constructor

File()

construct()

Creates a closed File that owns nothing yet: is_open() is false and every I/O method fails. Use File.open, File.create or File.open_with to get an open one.

Static methods

open

static open(path: Path): IoResult<File>

Opens an existing file for reading only. The position starts at 0.

A directory can be opened this way too, but reading it fails with is_is_a_directory().

Parameters

  • path — the file to open

Returns

  • the open File; an error with is_not_found() when the path is empty or does not exist, is_permission_denied() when access is refused, or another platform error

Example

    var r = File.open(Path("config.txt"));
    if (r.is_err() && r.error().is_not_found()) {
        return 0;
    }
    var text = r.value().read_string();

create

static create(path: Path): IoResult<File>

Opens a file for writing only, creating it if it is missing and truncating it to 0 bytes if it exists.

On POSIX a created file gets mode 0666 less the process umask.

Parameters

  • path — the file to create or truncate

Returns

  • the open File, empty and positioned at 0; an error with is_not_found() when the path is empty or its parent directory does not exist, is_permission_denied() when access is refused, or another platform error (on POSIX, is_is_a_directory() when the path is a directory)

Example

    var f = File.create(Path("report.txt")).value();
    f.write_all("done");

open_with

static open_with(path: Path, options: OpenOptions): IoResult<File>

Opens path as options describe. OpenOptions.open is the same call written as a builder.

The options are checked first, as in Rust: at least one of read, write or append is required, and create, create_new or truncate require write or append. The position starts at 0 (append mode still writes at the end).

Parameters

  • path — the file to open
  • options — the access mode and creation behavior

Returns

  • the open File; an error with is_invalid_input() when no access mode is set or create, create_new or truncate is set without write or append; is_not_found() when the path is empty, or the file (or a parent directory) is missing and neither create nor create_new is set; is_already_exists() when create_new is set and the path exists; is_permission_denied() when access is refused; or another platform error

Example

    var opts = OpenOptions().write(true).create_new(true);
    var r = File.open_with(Path("lock"), opts);
    if (r.is_err() && r.error().is_already_exists()) {
        return 1;
    }

std_file

static std_file(which: int, name: String): File

Returns a File for one of the process’s standard streams. The File does not own the handle, so neither close() nor the destructor closes the stream. stdin(), stdout() and stderr() are the usual way to call this.

On POSIX which is used directly as the file descriptor. On Windows it selects GetStdHandle(STD_INPUT_HANDLE - which), so only 0, 1 and 2 are meaningful there; a process without a console or redirection may get a null handle, and the File is then not open.

Parameters

  • which — the stream: 0 for standard input, 1 for standard output, 2 for standard error
  • name — the display name stored in the File’s path, such as <stdout>

Returns

  • a File on that stream, that does not close the stream when released

stdin

static stdin(): File

Returns a File reading the process’s standard input. Each call returns a new File on the same stream; the stream is never closed by a File. A read returns 0 at end of input (on Windows, also when the writing end of a pipe has closed).

Returns

  • a File on standard input, named <stdin>

stdout

static stdout(): File

Returns a File writing to the process’s standard output. Each call returns a new File on the same stream, and close() only marks that File closed: the stream stays usable. Writes are unbuffered, and each one first flushes what print has buffered, so output from print and from this File comes out in program order.

Returns

  • a File on standard output, named <stdout>

Example

    var out = File.stdout();
    out.write_all("hello");

stderr

static stderr(): File

Returns a File writing to the process’s standard error. Each call returns a new File on the same stream, and close() only marks that File closed: the stream stays usable. Writes are unbuffered, and each one first flushes what print has buffered.

Returns

  • a File on standard error, named <stderr>

read_bytes

static read_bytes(path: Path): IoResult<u8[]>

Reads the whole file at path into a byte array (Rust’s fs::read).

Parameters

  • path — the file to read

Returns

  • the file’s bytes; an error as for File.open (such as is_not_found()) or read_all

Example

    var r = File.read_bytes(Path("image.png"));
    if (r.is_ok()) {
        var n = r.value().count();
    }

read_to_string

static read_to_string(path: Path): IoResult<String>

Reads the whole file at path as UTF-8 text (Rust’s fs::read_to_string).

Parameters

  • path — the file to read

Returns

  • the file’s text; an error with is_invalid_input() when it is not valid UTF-8, or an error as for File.open (such as is_not_found()) or read_all

Example

    var r = File.read_to_string(Path("notes.txt"));
    if (r.is_err()) {
        return 1;
    }
    var text = r.value();

write_bytes

static write_bytes(path: Path, data: u8[]): IoResult<void>

Writes data as the whole contents of the file at path, creating it or replacing what it held (Rust’s fs::write), then closes it.

Not atomic: the file is truncated first, so a failure part way leaves it truncated or partly written.

Parameters

  • path — the file to write
  • data — the new contents

Returns

  • an Ok result once the data is written and the file closed; an error as for File.create (such as is_not_found() for a missing parent directory), write_all, or close

Example

    var data = Array<u8>();
    data.append(1 as u8);
    File.write_bytes(Path("one.bin"), data);

write_text

static write_text(path: Path, s: String): IoResult<void>

Writes s as UTF-8 as the whole contents of the file at path, creating it or replacing what it held, then closes it. No newline is added.

Not atomic: the file is truncated first, so a failure part way leaves it truncated or partly written.

Parameters

  • path — the file to write
  • s — the new contents

Returns

  • an Ok result once the text is written and the file closed; an error as for File.create (such as is_not_found() for a missing parent directory), write_all, or close

Note

  • this is the design proposal’s write_to_string; a static write would clash with the instance write

Example

    var r = File.write_text(Path("hello.txt"), "hello, world");
    if (r.is_err()) {
        return 1;
    }

copy

static copy(from: Path, to: Path): IoResult<ulong>

Copies the contents of the file from to to, creating to or truncating it first, in 64 KiB chunks.

Only the contents are copied: to keeps its own permissions and timestamps (a new file gets the defaults of File.create). A failure part way leaves to partly written.

Parameters

  • from — the file to copy
  • to — the destination file

Returns

  • the number of bytes copied; is_invalid_input() when from and to are the same file (after resolving symlinks), which truncating to would empty before it was read; otherwise an error as for File.open on from (such as is_not_found()), File.create on to, or a read, write or close failure

Example

    var n = File.copy(Path("a.txt"), Path("b.txt")).value();

rename

static rename(from: Path, to: Path): IoResult<void>

Renames or moves from to to, replacing an existing file at to (rename on POSIX, MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING on Windows).

Works for directories too. Moving between file systems (volumes) fails rather than copying.

Parameters

  • from — the existing path
  • to — the new path

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error with is_not_found() when from (or the parent of to) does not exist or, on POSIX, either path is empty, is_permission_denied() when access is refused, or another platform error

Example

    File.rename(Path("draft.txt"), Path("final.txt"));

remove

static remove(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Deletes the file at path. A symlink is removed itself, not its target. Directories are not removed: use Directory.remove or Directory.remove_all.

Parameters

  • path — the file to delete

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error with is_not_found() when the path does not exist (on POSIX, also when it is empty); when it is a directory, is_is_a_directory() on Linux and is_permission_denied() on macOS and Windows; is_permission_denied() when access is refused (on Windows also for a read-only file); or another platform error

Example

    var r = File.remove(Path("old.txt"));
    if (r.is_err() && !r.error().is_not_found()) {
        return 1;
    }

Methods

is_open

is_open(): bool

Returns whether the File holds a valid handle: true after a successful open, false after close() and for a File() never opened.

Returns

  • true while the File is open

check_open

check_open(): IoResult<void>

Checks that the File is open, for use before an operation.

Returns

  • an Ok result when the File is open; an error with the message “file is closed” otherwise (code EBADF on POSIX, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE on Windows; no IoError predicate holds)

read

read(buf: u8[], max: ulong): IoResult<ulong>

Reads up to max bytes from the current position and appends them to buf, growing it; the bytes already in buf are kept. Advances the position by the count read.

One system call: the read may be partial, returning fewer than max bytes before the end of the file (always so for pipes and terminals), and a single call moves at most about 2 GiB on POSIX or 1 GiB on Windows. Loop until it returns 0 to read everything, or use read_all. On POSIX an interrupted read (EINTR) is retried. On failure buf keeps its previous contents.

Parameters

  • buf — the array the bytes are appended to
  • max — the most bytes to read; 0 reads nothing and returns 0

Returns

  • the number of bytes appended, 0 at end of file; an error when the File is closed, or is_is_a_directory() when it is a directory, or another platform error

Example

    var buf = Array<u8>();
    while (true) {
        var r = f.read(buf, 4096);
        if (r.is_err() || r.value() == 0) {
            break;
        }
    }

read_all

read_all(): IoResult<u8[]>

Reads everything from the current position to the end of the file, in 64 KiB chunks, leaving the position at the end.

Returns

  • a new array of the bytes read (empty at end of file); an error when the File is closed, is_is_a_directory() when it is a directory, or another platform error, in which case the bytes read so far are discarded

read_string

read_string(): IoResult<String>

Reads everything from the current position to the end of the file, as read_all does, and returns it as UTF-8 text.

The bytes must be strictly valid UTF-8 (RFC 3629: no overlong forms, surrogates, or code points past U+10FFFF). A byte-order mark is kept as part of the text.

Returns

  • the text read (empty at end of file); an error with is_invalid_input() when the bytes are not valid UTF-8, or any error read_all returns

write

write(data: u8[]): IoResult<ulong>

Writes bytes from data at the current position (or at the end, in append mode) with a single system call, and advances the position.

The write may be partial: it can write fewer than data.count() bytes, and one call moves at most about 2 GiB on POSIX or 1 GiB on Windows. Use write_all to write everything. On POSIX an interrupted write (EINTR) is retried.

Parameters

  • data — the bytes to write

Returns

  • the number of bytes written, which may be less than data.count(); an error when the File is closed or was not opened for writing, or another platform error

write_all

write_all(data: u8[]): IoResult<void>

Writes all of data, repeating the write until every byte is written. Advances the position by data.count().

If an error occurs part of data may already have been written.

Parameters

  • data — the bytes to write

Returns

  • an Ok result once every byte is written; an error when the File is closed or was not opened for writing, when a write makes no progress (“failed to write the whole buffer”, with code EIO on POSIX or ERROR_WRITE_FAULT on Windows), or another platform error

write_all

write_all(s: String): IoResult<void>

Writes all of the UTF-8 bytes of s, as write_all does for bytes. No newline or terminator is added.

Parameters

  • s — the text to write

Returns

  • an Ok result once every byte is written; an error as for write_all(u8[])

Example

    var f = File.create(Path("greeting.txt")).value();
    var r = f.write_all("hello, world");
    if (r.is_err()) {
        return 1;
    }

write_string

[Deprecated("use 'write_all' instead", "write_all")] write_string(s: String): IoResult<void>

Deprecated: use write_all instead. Writes all of the UTF-8 bytes of s, exactly like write_all(s).

Parameters

  • s — the text to write

Returns

  • an Ok result once every byte is written; an error as for write_all

See also

  • write_all

seek_start

seek_start(pos: Offset): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position to pos bytes from the start of the file.

Seeking past the end is allowed; a later write there fills the gap with zeros.

Parameters

  • pos — the new position, in bytes from the start

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error as for seek

See also

  • seek

seek_end

seek_end(delta: Offset): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position to delta bytes from the end of the file. seek_end(0) moves to the end and returns the file’s length.

Parameters

  • delta — the offset from the end of the file, in bytes; negative moves back from the end

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error as for seek

See also

  • seek

seek_current

seek_current(delta: Offset): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position by delta bytes from where it is. seek_current(0) returns the current position without moving it.

Parameters

  • delta — the offset from the current position, in bytes; negative moves back

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error as for seek

See also

  • seek

seek

seek(offset: Offset, whence: int): IoResult<Offset>

Moves the position by offset relative to the origin whence. seek_start, seek_end and seek_current name the three origins.

A position before the start of the file is an error. Seeking a stream that has no position (a pipe or a terminal) fails on POSIX and has platform-defined results on Windows.

Parameters

  • offset — the offset in bytes from the origin; may be negative
  • whence — the origin: 0 the start of the file, 1 the current position, 2 the end of the file (SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, SEEK_END on POSIX; FILE_BEGIN, FILE_CURRENT, FILE_END on Windows)

Returns

  • the new position, in bytes from the start of the file; an error when the File is closed, whence is not 0, 1 or 2, the resulting position would be negative (on POSIX, with is_invalid_input()), or the stream cannot seek

set_length

set_length(size: ulong): IoResult<void>

Truncates or extends the file to exactly size bytes; bytes added are zeros. The position is kept, even when it is now past the end.

The File must have been opened for writing.

Parameters

  • size — the new length, in bytes

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the File is closed, was not opened for writing, or the system refuses the size

set_len

[Deprecated("use 'set_length' instead", "set_length")] set_len(size: ulong): IoResult<void>

Deprecated: use set_length instead. Truncates or extends the file to exactly size bytes.

Parameters

  • size — the new length, in bytes

Returns

  • the same as set_length(size)

sync

sync(): IoResult<void>

Flushes the file’s contents and metadata to the storage device, waiting until they are written (fsync on POSIX, FlushFileBuffers on Windows). Writes are already unbuffered in the process; this forces them out of the operating system’s cache.

On Windows the File must have been opened with write access.

Returns

  • an Ok result once the data is durable; an error when the File is closed or the device reports a failure, or another platform error

metadata

metadata(): IoResult<Metadata>

Queries the metadata of the open file itself (the target, when it was opened through a symlink): size, kind, read-only flag, permission bits and timestamps.

Returns

  • the file’s Metadata; an error when the File is closed, or another platform error

Example

    var size = f.metadata().value().size;

close

close(): IoResult<void>

Closes the File now, to observe the error the system reports (for example a deferred write failure). Without it the destructor closes the handle and ignores errors.

Idempotent: closing a closed File succeeds. The File counts as closed afterwards even when closing reports an error, so the handle is never closed twice. A standard stream is only marked closed: the stream stays open, and File.stdout() and the like still work.

Returns

  • an Ok result on success or when already closed; the platform error when closing an owned handle fails

Example

    var f = File.create(Path("out.bin")).value();
    f.write_all("data");
    if (f.close().is_err()) {
        return 1;
    }

Directory

Source: runtime/io/directory.pep

DirEntry

struct DirEntry

One entry of a directory listing, as Directory.entries() returns it.

The kind flags come from the listing itself and describe the entry without following symlinks. On POSIX a symlink has is_symlink set and is_file and is_directory clear; on Windows a symlink or junction to a directory has both is_directory and is_symlink set. Entries that are none of these (a FIFO, socket or device on POSIX) have all three flags clear. Call metadata() for the details of what the entry points to.

Example

    import io;

    var list = io.Directory.open(io.Path("src")).value().entries().value();
    ulong i = 0;
    while (i < list.count()) {
        if (list[i].is_file) {
            print(list[i].Name);
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }

Fields

path

Path path

The entry’s full path: the listed directory’s path joined with name (relative when the directory’s path was relative).

name

String name

The entry’s own file name, without any directory part.

is_file

bool is_file

Whether the entry is a regular file (never true for a symlink).

is_directory

bool is_directory

Whether the entry is a directory. On POSIX never true for a symlink; on Windows also true for a symlink or junction to a directory.

is_symlink

bool is_symlink

Whether the entry is a symlink (on Windows, any reparse point, junctions included), which is not followed.

Constructor

DirEntry()

construct()

Creates an empty entry: empty path and name, all kind flags false. Entries are normally obtained from Directory.entries().

Methods

metadata

metadata(): IoResult<Metadata>

Returns the metadata of the entry, following symlinks, exactly like Path.metadata() on the entry’s path. The file system is queried again now, so the result reflects any change since the listing was read.

Returns

  • the entry’s Metadata (of the target, for a symlink); an error when it cannot be stat’ed, with is_not_found() when the entry was removed since the listing or is a dangling symlink

See also

  • Path.metadata

Directory

struct Directory

A directory on the file system, identified by its path, together with static functions that create, remove and inspect directories and the process’s current and temporary directories.

A Directory holds no operating-system handle: open only checks that the path is a directory, and each call to entries() reads the listing afresh.

Example

    import io;

    var dir = io.Directory.temp().join("scratch").join("logs");
    if (io.Directory.create_all(dir).is_ok()) {
        var d = io.Directory.open(dir).value();
        var count = d.entries().value().count();
        io.Directory.remove_all(io.Directory.temp().join("scratch"));
    }

Fields

path

Path path

The directory’s path, as given to open.

Constructor

Directory()

construct()

Creates a Directory with an empty path, which names no directory. Use Directory.open to get one for an existing directory.

Static methods

open

static open(path: Path): IoResult<Directory>

Checks that path exists and is a directory (following symlinks) and returns a Directory for it. Nothing is kept open, so the directory can still be renamed or removed afterwards.

Parameters

  • path — the directory’s path; a relative path is resolved against the current directory whenever the Directory is used

Returns

  • the Directory; an error when path cannot be stat’ed (is_not_found() for a missing or empty path, is_permission_denied()) or is not a directory (is_not_a_directory(), message "not a directory")

Example

    import io;

    var d = io.Directory.open(io.Path("src"));
    if (d.is_err() && d.error().is_not_a_directory()) {
        print("src is a file");
    }

create

static create(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Creates one directory (mkdir on POSIX, with mode 0777 less the umask; CreateDirectoryW on Windows). Its parent must already exist.

Parameters

  • path — the directory to create

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the directory cannot be created: is_already_exists() when anything (a file too) is already at path, is_not_found() when the parent is missing or the path is empty, is_permission_denied() when the parent is not writable

See also

  • create_all

create_all

static create_all(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Creates a directory and any missing parents, like mkdir -p. Succeeds without doing anything when path is empty or already a directory (or a symlink to one). Parents are found lexically with Path.parent(); a relative path is created under the current directory. It is safe against another process creating the same directories at the same time.

Parameters

  • path — the directory to create, with its parents

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when a directory cannot be created: is_already_exists() when a file (not a directory) is at path or at one of its parents, is_permission_denied(), and so on. Parents created before the failure are left in place

Example

    import io;

    var r = io.Directory.create_all(io.Path("build").join("out").join("logs"));

remove

static remove(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Removes an empty directory (rmdir on POSIX, RemoveDirectoryW on Windows).

Parameters

  • path — the directory to remove; it must be empty

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when it cannot be removed: is_directory_not_empty() when it still has entries, is_not_found() when it is missing or the path is empty, is_not_a_directory() when path is a file, is_permission_denied()

See also

  • remove_all

remove_all

static remove_all(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Removes path and, if it is a directory, everything inside it, recursively. Symlinks are removed, never followed, so nothing outside the tree is touched. A file or symlink at path itself is simply removed.

Stops at the first failure, leaving whatever was not yet removed; on Windows a read-only file inside the tree is such a failure (is_permission_denied()).

Parameters

  • path — the file, symlink or directory tree to remove

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when something cannot be removed: is_not_found() when path does not exist (unlike rm -rf, a missing path is an error) or is empty, is_permission_denied(), and so on

See also

  • remove

Example

    import io;

    var tree = io.Directory.temp().join("my-scratch");
    var r = io.Directory.remove_all(tree);
    if (r.is_err() && !r.error().is_not_found()) {
        print(r.error().message);
    }

current

static current(): IoResult<Path>

Returns the process’s current directory, against which relative paths are resolved (getcwd on POSIX, GetCurrentDirectoryW on Windows).

Returns

  • the current directory as an absolute path; an error when it cannot be determined, such as is_not_found() on POSIX when the directory has been removed

See also

  • set_current

set_current

static set_current(path: Path): IoResult<void>

Changes the process’s current directory (chdir on POSIX, SetCurrentDirectoryW on Windows). This affects the whole process, every thread included: relative paths used anywhere afterwards resolve against the new directory.

Parameters

  • path — the new current directory; a relative path is resolved against the old one

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the directory cannot be entered: is_not_found() when it is missing or the path is empty, is_not_a_directory() when it is a file, is_permission_denied()

See also

  • current

temp

static temp(): Path

Returns the directory for temporary files. It is not created or checked, so it may not exist.

On POSIX it is $TMPDIR with any trailing / removed, or /tmp when TMPDIR is unset or empty. On Windows it is what GetTempPathW reports (from TMP, TEMP, USERPROFILE, or the Windows directory) with its trailing separator removed unless it is a root, or . if that call fails.

Returns

  • the temporary directory’s path, never an error

Example

    import io;

    var scratch = io.Directory.temp().join("my-tool");

Methods

entries

entries(): IoResult<DirEntry[]>

Reads the directory’s listing now, all at once: every entry except . and .., in the order the operating system returns them (not sorted). Uses opendir/readdir on POSIX and FindFirstFileW/FindNextFileW on Windows.

Returns

  • the entries, possibly none; an error when the directory cannot be read: is_not_found() when it no longer exists (or, on POSIX, path is empty), is_permission_denied(), or on POSIX is_not_a_directory() when path now names a file

Example

    import io;

    var list = io.Directory.open(io.Path(".")).value().entries();
    if (list.is_ok()) {
        var n = list.value().count();
    }

Network addresses

Network addresses: IpAddress (IPv4 or IPv6), SocketAddress (an IP address and a port), and resolve, which turns a host name into socket addresses.

Source: runtime/io/address.pep

IpAddress

struct IpAddress

An IPv4 or IPv6 address.

Make one with IpAddress.v4, IpAddress.v6, IpAddress.parse, or one of the well-known addresses (loopback_v4(), unspecified_v6(), …). IpAddress() is the IPv4 unspecified address 0.0.0.0.

to_string() prints IPv4 in dotted decimal (127.0.0.1) and IPv6 in the RFC 5952 form (::1, 2001:db8::8a2e:370:7334); an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address prints as ::ffff:1.2.3.4. An IPv4 address and the IPv6 address that maps it are different values.

See also

  • SocketAddress

Example

    import io;

    var a = io.IpAddress.parse("192.168.1.10").value();
    var b = io.IpAddress.v6(8193, 3512, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);   # 2001:db8::1
    print(a.is_v4());         # true
    print(b.to_string());     # 2001:db8::1

Constructor

IpAddress()

construct()

Creates the IPv4 unspecified address, 0.0.0.0.

Static methods

v4

Creates an IPv4 address from its four bytes, a.b.c.d.

Parameters

  • b — the second byte
  • c — the third byte
  • d — the fourth byte

Returns

Example

    var home = IpAddress.v4(127, 0, 0, 1);

v6

Creates an IPv6 address from its eight 16-bit groups, a:b:c:d:e:f:g:h.

Parameters

  • a — the first group

  • h — the eighth group

Returns

  • the address

Example

    var loopback = IpAddress.v6(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1);   # ::1

Returns the IPv4 unspecified address, 0.0.0.0. Binding to it listens on every IPv4 interface.

unspecified_v6

Returns the IPv6 unspecified address, ::. Binding to it listens on every IPv6 interface (and, where the system allows dual-stack sockets by default, such as Linux, on every IPv4 interface too).

parse

static parse(text: String): IoResult<IpAddress>

Parses an IPv4 address in dotted decimal (192.168.0.1) or an IPv6 address in the RFC 4291 text form (::1, fe80::1:2, ::ffff:10.0.0.1).

IPv4 needs exactly four decimal parts from 0 to 255 without leading zeros. IPv6 takes up to eight groups of one to four hex digits (either case), at most one ::, and an optional IPv4 address as the last 32 bits. Zone suffixes (%eth0), brackets and surrounding spaces are not accepted.

Parameters

  • text — the address to parse

Returns

  • the address; an error with is_invalid_input() when text is not a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address

Example

    var r = IpAddress.parse("10.0.0.300");
    print(r.is_err());   # true: 300 is out of range

Returns the address as text: dotted decimal for IPv4, the RFC 5952 form for IPv6 (lowercase hex, leading zeros dropped, the longest run of two or more zero groups written ::, ::ffff:a.b.c.d for an IPv4-mapped address).

Returns

SocketAddress

struct SocketAddress

An IP address and a port: where a socket is bound, or where it connects or sends.

Make one with SocketAddress(address, port) or SocketAddress.parse, or get a list from resolve. SocketAddress() is 0.0.0.0:0. The text form is address:port for IPv4 and [address]:port for IPv6.

    import io;

    var any = io.SocketAddress(io.IpAddress.unspecified_v4(), 8080);
    var local = io.SocketAddress.parse("[::1]:443").value();
    print(local.port());   # 443

resolve

resolve(host: String, port: u16): IoResult<SocketAddress[]>

Looks up the socket addresses of a host, with port attached to each.

A host that is already an IP address (as IpAddress.parse reads it) is returned as is, without a lookup. Anything else goes to the system resolver (getaddrinfo on POSIX, GetAddrInfoW on Windows), which consults the hosts file and DNS and blocks until it answers. The addresses come in the resolver’s order of preference, IPv4 and IPv6 mixed, each at most once.

Parameters

  • host — a host name such as "example.com" or "localhost", or an IP address
  • port — the port to put in every result

Returns

  • at least one address; an error with is_not_found() when the name has no address, is_invalid_input() when host is empty, or another resolver error

Example

    import io;

    var r = io.resolve("localhost", 8080);
    if (r.is_ok()) {
        for (var address in r.value()) {
            print(address.to_string());   # 127.0.0.1:8080, [::1]:8080, ...
        }
    }

Sockets

TCP and UDP sockets: TcpListener accepts connections, TcpStream is one connection, UdpSocket sends and receives datagrams.

Every call blocks the calling thread until it completes. Addresses are SocketAddress values; resolve turns a host name into them.

Source: runtime/io/socket.pep

TcpListener

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct TcpListener

A TCP socket that listens for connections.

TcpListener.bind opens one on a local address; each accept() waits for the next connection and returns it as a TcpStream together with the peer’s address. Binding to port 0 lets the system choose a free port; local_address() tells which.

On POSIX the listener sets SO_REUSEADDR, so a server can restart while connections from its previous run linger in TIME_WAIT. An IPv6 listener keeps the system’s default for accepting IPv4 too (on Linux and macOS it does, on Windows it does not).

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors. Every operation on a closed listener fails with an error no IoError predicate identifies (EBADF on POSIX, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE on Windows).

See also

  • TcpStream

Example

    import io;

    var listener = io.TcpListener.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("127.0.0.1:0").value()).value();
    print(listener.local_address().value().to_string());   # 127.0.0.1:<port>
    while (true) {
        var (stream, peer) = listener.accept().value();
        stream.write_string("hello " + peer.to_string());
    }

Returns

SharedTcpListener

[Shared] struct SharedTcpListener

A TCP listening socket that any thread can accept connections on: the thread-safe counterpart of TcpListener, for servers that accept on every worker of async.run at once (see async.spawn_on_each_worker). Each connection goes to one of the threads waiting in accept, and the stream it returns belongs to that thread.

A shared function may capture it. There is no close(), since another thread may be waiting on it: the socket closes when the last reference goes, which, for accept loops in tasks, is once async.run has cancelled them (accept then fails and the loop returns).

See also

  • TcpListener

Example

    import async;
    import io;

    main(): int {
        async.run(() => {
            var listener = io.SharedTcpListener.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("0.0.0.0:7000").value()).value();
            async.spawn_on_each_worker(() => {
                while (true) {
                    var accepted = listener.accept();
                    if (accepted.is_err()) {
                        return;
                    }
                    var (stream, peer) = accepted.value();
                    stream.write_string("hello");
                }
            });
        });
        return 0;
    }

Waits for the next incoming connection and returns it, as TcpListener.accept does. Several threads may wait at once; each connection wakes one of them (or, on some systems, several, and the rest keep waiting).

TcpStream

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct TcpStream

A TCP connection: a reliable, ordered stream of bytes in both directions.

Get one from TcpStream.connect (to an address), TcpStream.connect_host (to a host name) or TcpListener.accept. read appends what has arrived to a byte array and returns 0 once the peer has closed its side; write sends bytes.

Each call is one system call and blocks until it can make progress: a read returns as soon as some bytes are there, not when max bytes are, and a write may send fewer bytes than given. read_exact and write_all loop until done. Sending never raises SIGPIPE; writing to a connection the peer has closed fails with is_connection_reset().

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors. Every operation on a closed stream fails with an error no IoError predicate identifies (EBADF on POSIX, ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE on Windows).

See also

  • TcpListener

Example

    import io;

    var stream = io.TcpStream.connect_host("example.com", 80).value();
    stream.write_string("HEAD / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n");
    var reply = Array<u8>();
    while (stream.read(reply, 4096).value() > 0) {
    }

into_transfer

into_transfer(): SocketTransfer

Moves the connection out of this stream, into a token another thread can take it from with TcpStream.adopt. The stream is closed afterwards (is_open() is false), and a task waiting on it on this worker wakes with an error.

Inside async.run a socket belongs to the worker that uses it; this is how a task hands a connection to a task on another worker, such as one started with async.spawn.

Returns

  • the token; for a closed stream, one that adopt fails on

Example

    import async;
    import io;

    serve(listener: io.TcpListener) {
        var (stream, peer) = listener.accept().value();
        var transfer = stream.into_transfer();
        async.spawn<void>(() => {
            var mine = io.TcpStream.adopt(transfer).value();
            mine.write_string("hello from another worker");
        });
    }

close(): IoResult<void>

Closes the connection now. Closing a closed stream does nothing.

Returns

  • an Ok result on success or when already closed; the platform error when closing fails

SocketTransfer

[Shared] struct SocketTransfer

A connection on its way from one thread to another: made by TcpStream.into_transfer (or UnixStream.into_transfer), taken by TcpStream.adopt (or UnixStream.adopt, for a Unix domain connection). Unlike a stream, it is thread-safe, so a shared function (a body for async.spawn or Thread.spawn) can capture it and a Channel can carry it. If no one adopts it, the connection is closed when the last reference goes.

Constructor

Wraps a socket handle. TcpStream.into_transfer makes these; use it.

Parameters

  • handle — the socket, or an invalid handle for an empty token

UdpSocket

[NotCopyable("owns an operating-system socket and cannot be copied")] struct UdpSocket

A UDP socket: sends and receives datagrams, each delivered whole or not at all, in no guaranteed order.

UdpSocket.bind opens one on a local address (port 0 for any free port). send_to and receive_from name the peer on each call; after connect, send and receive use the connected peer and ignore datagrams from anyone else.

Each receive takes one datagram. A datagram longer than max is truncated to max bytes and the rest is lost, so size max for the largest datagram expected (at most 65507 bytes over IPv4).

Closing: the destructor closes the socket when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier and reports errors.

Example

    import io;

    var socket = io.UdpSocket.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("0.0.0.0:9000").value()).value();
    var buffer = Array<u8>();
    var (n, from) = socket.receive_from(buffer, 65507).value();
    socket.send_to(buffer, from);   # echo it back
