connect

connect(stream: io.TcpStream, host: String): io.IoResult<TlsStream>

Runs the TLS handshake as the client over stream and checks the server’s certificate.

Parameters

  • stream — a connected TCP stream; the TlsStream keeps it, and nothing else should read or write it afterwards
  • host — the name the certificate must be for, also sent to the server as the requested name (SNI); an IP address is checked against the certificate’s addresses instead

Returns

  • the encrypted stream; an error when the handshake fails or the certificate is not trusted (“certificate verify failed: …”), or an io error from the socket

connect_host

connect_host(host: String, port: u16): io.IoResult<TlsStream>

Connects to host on port with TcpStream.connect_host, then runs the handshake as connect does.

Parameters

  • host — a host name or an IP address
  • port — the port, usually 443

Returns

  • the encrypted stream; the errors of TcpStream.connect_host and of connect

TlsAcceptor

[Shared] struct TlsAcceptor

Accepts TLS server connections with one certificate.

An acceptor presents a certificate chain and its private key, read from PEM files. Each accept runs the TLS handshake over a TcpStream that a TcpListener accepted. Clients are not asked for certificates.

An acceptor is [Shared], so the accept loops of every worker can share one.

See also

  • TlsStream

Example

    import io;
    import tls;

    var acceptor = tls.TlsAcceptor.create(io.Path("cert.pem"), io.Path("key.pem")).value();
    var listener = io.TcpListener.bind(io.SocketAddress.parse("0.0.0.0:8443").value()).value();
    while (true) {
        var (tcp, peer) = listener.accept().value();
        var accepted = acceptor.accept(tcp);
        if (accepted.is_ok()) {
            accepted.value().write_string("hello over TLS");
        }
    }

TlsStream

[NotCopyable("owns a TLS connection and cannot be copied")] struct TlsStream

An encrypted connection: TLS over a TcpStream.

Get one from TlsConnector.connect or TlsAcceptor.accept. Reading and writing work as on a TcpStream, on the decrypted bytes: read appends what has arrived and returns 0 once the peer has closed the connection, write may send part of the data, and read_exact and write_all loop until done. In a task, a call that has to wait parks only the task.

shutdown() tells the peer that nothing more is coming (a TLS close_notify). A peer that closes the TCP connection without one also ends the stream: read returns 0.

Closing: the destructor closes the connection when the last reference goes; close() closes it earlier. Neither sends close_notify; call shutdown() first for that.

See also

  • TlsConnector
  • TlsAcceptor

Example

    var stream = connector.connect_host("localhost", 8443).value();
    stream.write_string("ping");
    var reply = Array<u8>();
    while (stream.read(reply, 4096).value() > 0) {
    }

is_open

is_open(): bool

Returns whether the stream is open.

Returns

read

read(buffer: u8[], max: ulong): io.IoResult<ulong>

Waits until data arrives, then appends up to max decrypted bytes of it to buffer.

Parameters

  • buffer — the array the bytes are appended to
  • max — the most bytes to read; 0 reads nothing and returns 0

Returns

  • the number of bytes appended, 0 once the peer has closed the connection; an error when the stream is closed, a TLS error, or an io error from the socket

read_exact

read_exact(buffer: u8[], count: ulong): io.IoResult<void>

Reads until exactly count more bytes are appended to buffer.

Parameters

  • buffer — the array the bytes are appended to
  • count — the number of bytes to read

Returns

  • an Ok result once count bytes are appended; an error when the connection ends first, or an error as for read. The bytes read before an error stay in buffer.

write

write(data: u8[]): io.IoResult<ulong>

Encrypts and sends bytes from data. The send may be partial; use write_all to send everything.

Parameters

  • data — the bytes to send

Returns

  • the number of bytes sent; an error when the stream is closed, a TLS error, or an io error from the socket

write_all

write_all(data: u8[]): io.IoResult<void>

Sends all of data, repeating the send until every byte is sent.

Parameters

  • data — the bytes to send

Returns

write_string

write_string(text: String): io.IoResult<void>

Sends all of the UTF-8 bytes of text, as write_all does.

Parameters

  • text — the text to send

Returns

shutdown

shutdown(): io.IoResult<void>

Tells the peer that nothing more is coming (sends a TLS close_notify). The peer’s reads return 0 after the data sent before.

Returns

  • an Ok result on success; an error when the stream is closed, or an io error from the socket

close

close(): io.IoResult<void>

Closes the connection now, without a close_notify (see shutdown). Closing a closed stream does nothing.

Returns

  • an Ok result on success or when already closed; the platform error when closing the socket fails

uri.pep

URI references (RFC 3986): parse any URI, such as https://example.com/a?b#c, mailto:someone@example.com or /items?page=2, into its parts.

Source: runtime/uri.pep

Uri

struct Uri

A URI reference split into its RFC 3986 components: scheme, authority (user information, host and port), path, query and fragment.

Uri.parse accepts any scheme, and a reference with no scheme (a relative reference, such as /items?page=2, which is what an HTTP server sees as a request’s target). The components keep their percent-escapes as written; Uri.decode turns an escaped component into text. The scheme is lowercased, since schemes are case-insensitive; nothing else is changed. to_string() puts the parts back together.

A component that can be absent is optional, so an empty one (http://h/? has an empty query) differs from a missing one (http://h/ has none).

Example

    var uri = Uri.parse("HTTPS://user@example.com:8443/a%20b?x=1#top").value();
    assert(uri.scheme == "https", "the scheme is lowercased");
    assert(uri.user_info.value() == "user", "user information");
    assert(uri.host.value() == "example.com", "host");
    assert(uri.port.value() == 8443, "port");
    assert(uri.path == "/a%20b", "the path keeps its escapes");
    assert(Uri.decode(uri.path).value() == "/a b", "decoded");
    assert(uri.query.value() == "x=1" && uri.fragment.value() == "top", "query and fragment");

Fields

scheme

var scheme: String

The scheme, lowercased, such as https; empty for a relative reference.

user_info

var user_info: String?

The user information before @ in the authority, if any.

host

var host: String?

The host, without the brackets of an IPv6 address; None when the URI has no authority (no //), and empty for one such as file:///tmp.

port

var port: u16?

The port after the host, if the authority gives one.

path

var path: String

The path, possibly empty, with its percent-escapes.

query

var query: String?

The query after ?, without the ?, if any.

fragment

var fragment: String?

The fragment after #, without the #, if any.

Constructor

Uri()

construct()

Creates an empty relative reference: no scheme, no authority, and an empty path.

Static methods

parse

static parse(text: String): Result<Uri>

Parses text as a URI reference: an absolute URI with any scheme, or a relative reference.

Characters outside printable ASCII (spaces, controls, and every non-ASCII byte) must be percent-encoded, and each % must be followed by two hexadecimal digits.

Parameters

  • text — the URI reference

Returns

  • the parsed URI, or an error saying what is wrong: an invalid scheme, a character that must be encoded, a bad escape, an IPv6 host with no ], or a port that is not a number from 0 to 65535

Example

    var mail = Uri.parse("mailto:someone@example.com").value();
    assert(mail.scheme == "mailto" && mail.host.is_none(), "no authority");
    assert(mail.path == "someone@example.com", "the path holds the address");
    assert(Uri.parse("a b").is_err(), "a space must be encoded");

decode

static decode(text: String): Result<String>

Returns text with each percent-escape (%20) replaced by the byte it stands for, decoded as UTF-8. A + is kept as it is; a query that uses + for a space needs that replaced first.

Parameters

  • text — a component with percent-escapes, such as path

Returns

  • the decoded text, where each byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD, the replacement character, or an error when a % is not followed by two hexadecimal digits

Example

    assert(Uri.decode("caf%C3%A9%21").value() == "café!", "decoded");
    assert(Uri.decode("100%").is_err(), "a lone '%'");

Methods

is_absolute

is_absolute(): bool

Returns whether this URI has a scheme (an absolute URI rather than a relative reference).

Returns

  • true when scheme is not empty

authority

authority(): String?

Returns the authority as it appears after //: user information, host (in brackets when it is an IPv6 address) and port.

Returns

  • the authority, such as user@example.com:8443, or None when host is None

path_and_query

path_and_query(): String

Returns the path and query, as an HTTP request line names its target: the path (/ when it is empty), then ? and the query if there is one. The fragment is left out.

Returns

  • the path and query, such as /items?page=2

to_string

to_string(): String

Returns the URI as text, putting its components back together. For a parsed URI this is the text it was parsed from, except that the scheme is lowercased.

Returns

  • the URI reference as a String

Building this documentation

This book lives in docs/ and is rendered with mdBook. The standard library reference (docs/src/reference/) is generated from the runtime’s doc comments by pepper-docgen, a tool in this repository.

cargo install mdbook --locked                 # once

cargo run -p pepper-docgen -- serve           # live preview while writing
cargo run -p pepper-docgen -- reference       # regenerate the reference after changing runtime docs
cargo run -p pepper-docgen -- build           # render into target/docs-site/dev/
cargo run -p pepper-docgen -- build --version 0.2.0 --site <dir>

Keeping the book current

Documentation changes land in the same PR as the code they describe. The checklist of what to update for each kind of change is in AGENTS.md, under “Keep the documentation current”.

Examples are tested

Every runnable example lives in docs/examples/: a single name.pep, or a folder name/ whose entry point is main.pep. Chapters pull them in with mdBook’s include syntax, so the text on the page is the file that was tested:

```pepper
{{#include ../../examples/structs.pep}}
```

crates/pepper-driver/tests/integration/docs_examples_tests.rs compiles and runs every example; each must return 0 from main and uses assert to check what it shows. Short fragments that are not whole programs can stay inline in the chapter.

Versions

Documentation is versioned with the compiler’s semantic version (version in the root Cargo.toml). pepper-docgen build --version X.Y.Z renders the book into <site>/X.Y.Z/ and leaves every other version in the site alone; versions.json lists them for the version picker, and the site’s index.html opens the newest release. Builds from main publish as dev.

The Docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yml) publishes to the gh-pages branch: pushing to main updates dev, and pushing a tag vX.Y.Z adds the X.Y.Z docs. Published versions are never deleted.

The reference stays current

cargo run -p pepper-docgen -- check fails when docs/src/reference/ does not match the runtime, and CI runs it. The runtime itself must meet the doc comment standard in AGENTS.md, which runtime_docs_tests.rs enforces.
